 Russell Brand to be Sentenced For Rape And Sexual Assault
 BBC News
 Close Watch live here from 13:45 Contains some upsetting scenes. Summary
 Warning: This page contains distressing details 
 Russell Brand is being sentenced for rape and three counts of sexual assault , after being found guilty at Southwark Crown Court on Thursday
 One victim tells the court she was "in shock and turmoil... I didn't have any respect for myself" 
 Another victim says "Russell Brand is a sexual predator who has no remorse" , while another says she "felt powerless in that moment" 
 The woman who Brand raped in 2009 tells the court she is "living with trauma" , and feared she had contracted HIV 
 In mitigation before sentencing, Brand's lawyer says his client is "a fundamentally different person today" 
 You'll be able to watch the sentencing itself live on this page from 14:00 GMT - before then, our team is reporting from inside the court 
 In total, Brand faced seven charges: three of rape, three of sexual assault and one of attempted indecent assault. He was found not guilty on three counts
 His crimes took place between 2004 and 2009, and related to four women. They are all entitled to lifelong anonymity

 2:07 Met Police release Brand interview footage. 00:02:07, play video Met Police release Brand interview footage

 Live Reporting
 Edited by Imogen James and Alex Smith, with Helena Wilkinson and Sima Kotecha at Southwark Crown Court. Warning: this page contains distressing details
 Hearing breaks and will return at 14:00 GMT published at 12:36 GMT 12:36 GMT 
 Sima Kotecha 
Reporting from Southwark Crown Court 
 The judge says he will now rise and he will return at 14:00 GMT.
 Brand looks back at his wife as he exits the dock. She mouths: "I love you."
 As a reminder, you'll be able to watch the judge's sentencing remarks live on this page. 
 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Lawyer highlights Brand's charity work published at 12:34 GMT 12:34 GMT 
 Sima Kotecha 
Reporting from Southwark Crown Court 
 Defence barrister Ian Winter KC says Brand has spent a lot of time since the mid-2000s working with a variety of rehab charities.
 Winter says Brand raised a large amount of money for his charity work over the years - in 2015 he opened a cafe in Hoxton in order to help former prisoners and those struggling with addiction.
 "A lot of people have been helped in life-saving ways by Mr Brand’s care for them," Winter says.
 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Brand's lawyer says his wife is experiencing 'total devastation' published at 12:28 GMT 12:28 GMT 
 Helena Wilkinson 
Reporting from Southwark Crown Court 
 Winter says Russell Brand's wife of ten years is at court today, and is experiencing "total devastation".
 The defence barrister adds that the couple are "wrestling" with how to explain to one of their children - who is 10 years old - what has happened. 
 He says the consequences of Brand's conduct to totally innocent people should be put into the equation when the judge reaches a sentence.
 Image source, PA Media Image caption, Laura Brand pictured arriving at court this morning
 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Being 'tipsy' doesn't mean vulnerable, says Brand's barrister published at 12:25 GMT 12:25 GMT 
 Sima Kotecha 
Reporting from Southwark Crown Court 
 Brand's barrister Ian Winter KC is now talking in reference to the victim who Brand sexually assaulted at a bar, when he grabbed her breasts in 2004.
 He argues that being "tipsy" shouldn’t be considered as being vulnerable.
 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Rape victim 'not particularly vulnerable', Brand's lawyer says published at 12:24 GMT 12:24 GMT 
 Claire Ellison 
Reporting from Southwark Crown Court 
 The defence barrister now argues the woman who Brand anally raped was "not particularly vulnerable - she must have felt sufficiently confident [going to his house], considering the sort of persona, and the sort of sex he would engage in".
 As a reminder, the role of Brand's barrister is to outline any mitigating features on behalf of his client that he thinks should be considered by the judge, in order to reduce the sentence. 
 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Rape was 'momentary failure to respect consent', defence argues published at 12:17 GMT 12:17 GMT 
 Helena Wilkinson 
Reporting from Southwark Crown Court 
 Defence barrister Ian Winter KC is making submissions to the court about their view on what should be considered when reaching a sentence.
 On the rape conviction, Winter says it occurred after "fully consensual vaginal intercourse" and "was quite a short... momentary total failure to respect her consent".
 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Brand a 'fundamentally different person today', defence argues published at 12:10 GMT 12:10 GMT 
 Helena Wilkinson 
Reporting from Southwark Crown Court 
 Russell Brand's defence barrister, Ian Winter KC, is now on his feet.
 Winter says Brand "is a fundamentally different person today" and points out the rape took place 17 years ago.
 These incidents occurred at a point in his career when Brand was very famous, Winter says.
 He adds that Brand's crimes were connected to that exposure to fame.
 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Brand appears pale and keeps closing his eyes published at 12:03 GMT 12:03 GMT 
 Sima Kotecha 
Reporting from Southwark Crown Court 
 Russell Brand’s hair is shorter than it was last week.
 He appears pale. He closes his eyes every so often. 
 His wife Laura stretches her neck as she tries to catch a glimpse of his face from behind the dock
 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Prosecution outlines mitigating factors published at 12:02 GMT 12:02 GMT 
 Helena Wilkinson 
Reporting from Southwark Crown Court 
 While still addressing Brand's rape conviction, the prosecutor says they have identified mitigating factors.
 These are Brand's "good character" as there is an absence of any recent convictions, apart from his previous conviction for possession of cannabis.
 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Prosecutor says victim was vulnerable published at 12:01 GMT 12:01 GMT 
 Helena Wilkinson and Sima Kotecha 
Reporting from Southwark Crown Court 
 The prosecutor now turns to culpability. 
 Riel Karmy-Jones KC says based on what they submit, the starting point for the rape conviction is 12 years in custody. 
 Remember there are other steps the judge will need to consider including aggravating and mitigating features.
 The prosecution counsel asks the court to adjust the sentencing by taking aggravating features into account. 
The barrister says the victim was vulnerable.
 She says a condom was removed without the victim's consent, and argues the location of the offence - Brand’s former home - is an aggravating feature.
 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Brand knew rape victim 'idolised' him, prosecution says published at 11:57 GMT 11:57 GMT 
 Claire Ellison 
Reporting from Southwark Crown Court 
 The prosecution says the woman - who Brand was convicted of raping - "did idolise him and was star struck". 
 Brand knew that, says the prosecutor. He was a much older man and he pursued her through text messages and phone calls, the prosecutor adds. 
 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Prosecution says Brand's crimes have had 'extreme impact' published at 11:56 GMT 11:56 GMT 
 Helena Wilkinson 
Reporting from Southwark Crown Court 
 The prosecutor is addressing Brand's rape conviction. Riel Karmy-Jones KC says the prosecution submit it falls into category one. 
 "We submit there has been an extreme impact," she says. 
 She adds that the woman was also exposed to "degradation" and "humiliation". Brand told her to shower and brush teeth, and after raping her told her to "clear up the mess". 
 The prosecution counsel alleges that Brand "manipulated her into coming to his house that day".
 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Rape victim suffered 'significant psychological harm', prosecution says published at 11:50 GMT 11:50 GMT 
 Sima Kotecha 
Reporting from Southwark Crown Court 
 More now on the considerations for sentencing. 
 The prosecution counsel talks about the medical records of the rape victim - saying that the attack had harmed her, and that she was worried about contracting HIV.
 She said, taking that into account, "there is sufficient evidence for the court to find there has been significant psychological harm".
 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Prosecutor turns to sentencing framework published at 11:48 GMT 11:48 GMT 
 Helena Wilkinson 
Reporting from Southwark Crown Court 
 We've now heard all four victim impact statements, and the prosecutor says she will now turn to the sentencing framework. 
 It is the prosecutor's role during a sentencing hearing to assist the court to reach the most appropriate sentence for Brand, she says. 
 The Sentencing Council’s rape guidelines provide an offence range of four to 19 years’ custody, although sentences of 20 years or more may be appropriate for exceptionally serious cases.
 For a sexual assault offence the range is from a community order to seven years in prison. 
 Sometimes judges can sentence outside the normal range.
 For each offence the judge will have to look at Brand’s alleged culpability and the harm caused.
 He'll also take into account any factors which may increase or reduce the sentences. 
 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 'I felt my working environment wasn't safe,' says sexual assault victim published at 11:46 GMT 11:46 GMT 
 Helena Wilkinson and Sima Kotecha 
Reporting from Southwark Crown Court 
 The prosecution reads a statement from another victim - the woman who was sexually assaulted while working on a Channel 4 project with Brand in 2009.
 It's the fourth victim impact statement we've heard today.
 She says that following the incident she was "really upset" and felt she "lost my trust in people".
 "I felt my working environment wasn’t safe," she says, adding: "I felt powerless in that moment."
 As the impact of Brand's crimes on the women are heard in court, he looks straight ahead in the dock. He appears to be listening intently. 
 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Rape victim was worried her identity would become known during trial published at 11:45 GMT 11:45 GMT 
 Claire Ellison 
Reporting from Southwark Crown Court 
 The statement continues, with the woman saying she was unprepared for the publicity of this trial, and was worried throughout that her identity would become known.
 Characterisations that she was simply an "obsessive fan" were "deeply hurtful", she says in her statement.
 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Victim says there was a 'power imbalance' published at 11:43 GMT 11:43 GMT 
 Helena Wilkinson 
Reporting from Southwark Crown Court 
 The prosecutor continues reading a statement from the woman Brand was convicted of raping in 2009. 
 "The incident has affected my relationships," she says in her statement.
 The woman says one of the worst parts of what happened was her fear that she might have contracted HIV.
 After the incident she was in significant pain, the statement reads.
 "The defendant's public profile had a significant impact on me", she says - adding that because of who Brand was she didn't feel confident to speak out about what happened. 
 "His fame... wealth created a power imbalance," she says, and his public profile made it difficult for her to move on.
 "He was so powerful, rich and influential."
 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 'I am living with trauma... something I carry every day', says rape victim published at 11:36 GMT 11:36 GMT 
 Sima Kotecha 
Reporting from Southwark Crown Court 
 The prosecution is now delivering a statement from the woman who Brand was convicted of anally raping in 2009, after meeting her at a comedy show in Hammersmith.
 This is the third victim impact statement we've heard in court.
 She says she "struggled to sleep and eat" and to "cope with my emotions" after the attack.
 The victim says she had to take time away from work and live with her parents. "I am living with trauma and something I carry every day", she tells the court.
 The woman's confidence and self esteem have been "badly affected" and she no longer trusts her instincts, she says.
 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Assault had a 'lasting impact on my life', says victim in statement published at 11:33 GMT 11:33 GMT 
 Sima Kotecha 
Reporting from Southwark Crown Court 
 The prosecution counsel now reads a statement from another victim, who was sexually assaulted by Brand in 2005.
 She says while Brand has "managed to move on" that this "has had a lasting impact on my life".
 She adds that "over the years, hearing his voice on television or seeing his image has made me jump."
 The statement ends with: "Russell Brand is a sexual predator who has no remorse... I just hope he is not allowed to hurt any more women."
 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Victim says 'a leopard may change its spots, but it’s still a leopard' published at 11:29 GMT 11:29 GMT 
 Helena Wilkinson 
Reporting from Southwark Crown Court 
 The victim finishes off her statement by saying: "I just want to say - a leopard may change its spots, but it’s still a leopard."
 The judge praises her for her courage.
